title: The Dead Village
timelinePosition: Directly after Chapter 2's final approach to Millhaven. Chapter 2 closed in fading light after a night-and-day ride with no sleep.
openLocation: Millhaven, first human village south of the Quel'Thalas borderlands
transport: Mounted approach on Thalassian horses; on foot during the village sweep
immediateObjective: Sweep Millhaven, learn what happened to its people, and decide whether the threat is moving toward Quel'Thalas.
constraints: Absolute limited third on Sylvanas; nothing she could not perceive or infer
Jaina stays 'the mage' in Sylvanas's narration for the whole chapter (partnership-arc marker); she does not grow warm, she just stops treating the read as optional
Open on silence and procedure, not another fight (Ch 2 closed on three violent or dread beats)
No confirmation that grain carries the sickness: the granary reads loudest and Jaina refuses to treat it as the answer
No proof of an organized cult behind it; dead moving north is a direction, not a command structure
The old carter reads as ordinary, useful and forgettable; Sylvanas builds no case around him or his farewell
The grain-seller mention is a weak, unresolved clue: heard once, not connected
Second read of Beat 9 is plant only; the prose must not explain it
Keep consistent with Ch 2 B11: the deer was wounded and still on its feet, not reanimated; the sickness is active in living flesh before death
Fatigue registers for both women after a ride with no sleep
Neral and the unnamed ranger leave the book's southbound party at Beat 8; the survivor girl never continues south
Lyriel's carter answer is warm and true and must not sound careless

worldbuildingReferences: stories/the-plague-road/locations/lordaeron-and-northrend.md (border country, Millhaven: crossroads, mill, tavern, a few dozen lives)

castKnowsLeavingChapter: Millhaven is the first village on this road fully taken

pov: She opens treating this as a border problem to read and report, not a human disaster she has to carry herself.
The silent village and the missing bodies force her to read tracks, corpses, and magic together.
She starts the chapter using Jaina as a specialist, not a partner.
By the end, Sylvanas still does not trust Jaina, but she stops treating the mage's read as optional.

beats: Sylvanas expects Jaina to be good at magic and weak on the actual road.
Jaina proves more useful than that by helping separate the loudest wrongness from the real pattern.
Sylvanas does not grow warm, but she starts listening when Jaina speaks.

team.label: Partnership
beats: They begin as a custody escort with no trust between them.
Millhaven forces them to build one picture out of physical and magical evidence.
They do not soften. They just stop wasting time pretending the other half of the problem does not matter.

castAndHandoffRules: Cyndia: remains with the riding party. She is the ranger Sylvanas trusts most on the ground.
Lyriel: remains with the riding party. She talks to anyone on a road, and she is the one who answers the carter.
Neral: present at open. She rescues the survivor girl and rides north with the warning dispatch in this chapter.
Unnamed escort ranger: rides north with Neral and the survivor girl.
Survivor girl: found in a cellar. Escorted north by Neral. Does not continue south.
Old carter: helpful local source on the road. He should read ordinary, useful, and forgettable.
Next chapter starts: Chapter 4 opens after a two-day ride south with Sylvanas, Jaina, Cyndia, and Lyriel.

scenes.title: Millhaven
scenes.sceneFunction: They enter the first village the plague has truly emptied and realize the missing dead are the real problem.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The contamination is real and the party arrives at Millhaven after a ride with no sleep, but they still don't know how it got here. Ch 2 showed it active in living animals before death. Sylvanas holds Jaina as a specialist, 'the mage', not a partner.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas defaults to physical procedure and her own training; Jaina's magical read has to earn a place beside it.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only: Millhaven is the first alarm-bell village, crossroads, mill, tavern, a few dozen lives, doors open and people gone (lordaeron-and-northrend.md); border country is mud, grey-green woods, livestock, woodsmoke, autumn harvest. Thalassian horses are trained to tolerate ward hum and settle fast, so a horse that will not settle is itself a signal (thalassian-horses.md). No web research run; no canon source for Millhaven's layout beyond these notes, so mill, well, granary and cellar placement is planner inference.

beats.goal: Enter Millhaven and secure it by procedure: read the silence, set a perimeter and order a full physical sweep before anyone relies on the mage's senses.
beats.conflict: Nothing to fight and nothing to see. No voices, animals or work sounds; the wrongness is thick enough to unsettle trained Thalassian horses; the party is tired and every closed door could hide a living thing or a bad surprise.

outcome.summary: Sylvanas gets her sweep ordered and the party deployed in pairs, but the village gives up no danger and no answer, only the sense that it stopped mid-day.

Verifier should decide the arrival hour; the writer should not state clock time that contradicts Ch 2. Keep 'recent collapse' without a specific hour of day, and let tired light carry through.

beats.goal: Find the dead or the kill site: bodies, blood, a stand point, any reading of how the village fell.
beats.conflict: There is nothing. Every house shows people leaving the middle of ordinary life and not returning; the village emptied slowly, not in one panicked attack. No bodies to study means no wounds, no cause and no count.

outcome.summary: No kill site, no corpses, and three bad possibilities (fled, taken, or rose and walked out); Sylvanas has nothing physical to read, so Jaina turns to the places that hold the most magic.

beats.interiority: Sylvanas has seen sacked towns; this is not that. A town does not simply stop. Keep the cat in mind: animals that are fine, people that are gone. She is counting what is missing, not what is there.
beats.plannerWarning: Ch 2 B11 established the plague active in animals; the barn cat's health is ambiguous. Write it as plainly ordinary, healthy-looking and indifferent, not a sign of immunity or pattern.

beats.goal: Get Jaina's reading of the most saturated sites (well, cellar, granary, soil) while Sylvanas holds the sightlines, and find the source of the sickness.
beats.conflict: The whole village is soaked and the loudest site does not mean the first one. The granary reads strongest of all, but Jaina refuses to call the loudest residue the whole answer; to Sylvanas, that restraint could be caution or performance.

outcome.summary: Magic shows the scale and the saturation, but no clean origin; Sylvanas notices the mage's discipline and begins, a little, to trust her judgment, while still needing tracks to know where it went.

scenes.title: The Survivor and the Proof
scenes.sceneFunction: They find a living child in the wreck of the village and turn horror into physical proof they can send north.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The village is dead and the bodies are gone; the dead left on their feet but no direction is certain. They still need proof of where the threat moved next, and they do not yet know any witnesses live.
scenes.arcPressure: The physical evidence and the magical read have to be combined into one picture; this is the scene where Sylvanas lets the mage strip noise from the ground.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only: Neral is the early third ranger and northbound dispatch rider, structural use is getting warnings out and escorting the survivor (supporting.md); voice sheet governs her manner. Plague notes: dead rise at death after repeated ingestion and answer as a 'choir', crude convergence, rough answerability (plague-mechanism.md), which supports 'rough formation' without a commander. No web research run. The 'at least sixty' count is the outline's number, not sourced.

beats.goal: Get the hidden child out of the cellar alive and calm enough to speak, without frightening her back into the dark.
beats.conflict: She is dehydrated, terrified and barely able to speak; she trusts only Neral; the cellar is cramped and the party is unsure whether anything else is down there with her.

outcome.summary: The girl is alive and confirms people died here and something happened at night, but she is fragile and her memory may be broken.

beats.goal: Pull a usable account from the girl: what happened, when, and which way the dead went.
beats.conflict: She remembers pieces, not a narrative; terror may distort route and order; Sylvanas will not accept a child's word as proof without the ground matching it; Jaina has to separate fear from the useful magical detail.

outcome.summary: Fragments line up: sweetness on people's breath, sick neighbors, the dead rising and dragging north at night, and a newer grain seller mentioned in passing; the pieces point north, but terror might be bending the route.

outcome.summary: The ground confirms the girl: at least sixty bodies moved north-northeast toward the border in rough formation, turning the threat into a direct border warning; but nothing explains what raised them or who leads them.

scenes.title: The Old Carter on the Road
scenes.sceneFunction: Sylvanas sends the warning north, crosses paths with a casually helpful old carter, and commits her remaining force to riding south.
scenes.knowledgeAtSceneStart: The dead are confirmed moving north. The survivor has to leave right away with the dispatch. Sylvanas must now weigh the border against the south.
scenes.arcPressure: Sylvanas chooses the border over her own comfort and then chooses to keep following Jaina's trail rather than fall back; she tells herself it is the trail, not the mage.
scenes.enrichment: Project notes only: the carter is the Mal'Ganis plant (investigation-arc.md; lyriel-voice.md fixes her answer: she tells him they passed nobody, mentions the girl's grain-seller, says they will watch for him going south, and that he would get a better price going home full). Cyndia hears the odd farewell here and again in Ch 15 as independent corroboration (cyndia.md), so she should be within earshot. Lordaeron border country is farmland, mud, livestock, harvest (lordaeron-and-northrend.md). No web research run. Mal'Ganis's identity and the downstream consequences (Ch 5 depot, Ch 9 ward) are plant-only in this chapter and come from project notes, not canon.

beats.emotion: Tight, cold urgency: the theory has become a cellar, a child and sixty feet of ground, and she resents how much of this is now hers to carry.
beats.dilemma: Keep the full escort and risk the dispatch arriving late, or strip her own force to guarantee the warning and the child reach the border.
beats.decision: She sends Neral north with the girl, the dispatch and the extra escort, cutting her own strength to four for the ride south.

Writer: 'prisoner' as a thought about status is fine, but Jaina stays 'the mage' in narration. Also: 'the one who knows where to go' should land as Sylvanas's irritation, not a trust concession.

beats.conflict: The man is plain, helpful and sincere; his information is real but too normal to flag anything; he keeps looking past them toward Millhaven; his grain-man question is road gossip and Lyriel answers him as she answers anyone.

outcome.summary: They get a plain, useful read on the settlements south, still trading and alive, and Lyriel's friendly answer closes the exchange; nothing looks wrong, and that is the problem.
